result.reviewScopeSummary: Verified Story 0 against the story, the full Session Context Store tech design, and the test plan, then checked the implemented foundation modules, shared test scaffolding, verification scripts, direct foundation tests, and the installed PI type contracts before running the targeted, story, and epic gates.

newFindings.title: Shared PI fixture builders do not match the installed PI message contracts
newFindings.evidence: Story 0 puts test fixture builders in scope for downstream stories and the test plan says PI-facing tests should use typed fixtures that match PI event/session shapes (`00-foundation.md` lines 29-33 and 118-120; `test-plan.md` lines 11-19 and 38-51). In `src/context-steward/test/fixtures.ts`, the local PI fixture types diverge from the installed contracts: `PiToolCallContentBlockFixture` uses `type: "tool-call"` plus `toolCallId`/`toolName`/`input` (lines 51-56), but the real `ToolCall` is `type: "toolCall"` with `id`/`name`/`arguments` (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/types.d.ts` lines 117-123); `PiImageContentBlockFixture` uses `url` (lines 58-61), while real image content uses `data`/`mimeType` (types.d.ts lines 112-116); and `PiAssistantMessageFixture` / `PiToolResultMessageFixture` omit required upstream fields such as `api`, `usage`, and `timestamp` (fixtures lines 80-95 vs types.d.ts lines 144-166). `tests/context-steward/foundation.test.ts` lines 22-160 only prove helper determinism and schema defaults, so this scaffolding contract gap is invisible to the passing gates.

`npm run verify-all` reported `No integration tests found.`, which is consistent with Chunk 0's planned 0 TC / 2 non-TC scope and is not the blocking issue here.

The reviewed `src/context-steward` tree stays within Story 0 scope: only shared `domain/` and `test/` modules are present, with no early thread-store, capture, turn, import, repair, or fixture runtime implementation.
